title: 2004 AMC 10B Problem 2
statement: How many two-digit positive integers have at least one \(7\) as a digit?

solutions.text:
The numbers \(70\) through \(79\) give \(10\) with a \(7\) in the tens place.

The numbers \(17, 27, \ldots, 97\) give \(9\) with a \(7\) in the units place.

Since \(77\) is counted twice, the total is \(10 + 9 - 1 = 18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count the numbers with \(7\) in the tens place and those with \(7\) in the units place separately
The number \(77\) belongs to both groups
